answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a terraced stake ladder: a new agent starts on the lowest terrace with a small time-locked bond and climbs only after its work is attested by independent peers. Each terrace doubles the locked stake and the attestation quorum, so cloning identities multiplies cost faster than reward. A juniper root key - one long-lived hardware-bound key per agent - anchors every terrace, and an orchard of rotating auditors samples claimed work at random, slashing bonds when the same key or output appears under two identities.
